items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band

ctx.x: Be integrated more? Yeah, it should be. Well you know they have it in the smaller groups they don’t have the big bands really to mix it more, with more, because we don’t have big bands. But that’s one thing that they never paid much attention to, you know? Of course © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Benny would do what he wanted to do, and so did Jimmy, Jimmy Dorsey. He had a girl named, black girl named June Richmond and boy she could sing, boy. And he brought her from California all through Texas and everywhere with him. So you’ve got to give him credit for that. This was Jimmy, not Tommy, Jimmy, his brother, you know? And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band, and Sy Oliver was writing all these arrangements. So there was more integration, more. Of course we had more musicians and as I…
A couple of last questions I would like to ask you. Was the Basie band the best big band there ever was?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: he was working with Tommy Dorsey

ctx.x: came to town. I said, "Basie, don't worry." By this time, Prez was drinking like a quart of Granddad a day. I says, "Man, they don't want Prez. His health won't allow it." I says, "I don't think he's healthy enough for the Army." I says, "And you know they don't want Jo because he's crazy." That's just what I said. Shit, two days, man, they had them in Fort Ord. That was a little old Army place right out of Los Angeles. They were mad with them and two days, they had them in Fort Ord.

So Artie Shaw had just given up the Navy band. They dropped a bomb close to him over -- they had a hell of a Navy band in the Navy. So he told them, he says, "I don't care what you do to me or how you feel about it," he says, "I'm going." He said, "Just put me in the brig," he says, "because I'm not going to play anymore." So they let him out and he was in California. We were doing command performances and he and Basie were tight. So he says, "Bill, I can play Prez' parts on clarinet." So we had him. He played…
